source.title: Maximum Product of Three Elements After One Replacement

teaching.hint: How much freedom does the replacement give over the sign and magnitude of one chosen factor?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The replacement can have maximum magnitude and whichever sign makes the best untouched pair nonnegative.
solution_outline.approach: Find the two largest absolute values among original elements. Replace a third index by an endpoint value with the sign that makes their product nonnegative.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The chosen pair is untouched and maximizes the absolute product of any two originals; a distinct third index exists.
solution_outline.correctness: The construction attains `100000` times the largest absolute pair product. Any final triple contains at most one replaced element; if it omits that element, one original factor is also at most `100000` in magnitude, so the same value bounds it.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space, with wide multiplication.
solution_outline.pitfall: Replacing one of the best pair values needlessly loses the distinct-index construction.

common_wrong_turns: Assuming the replacement must be positive
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained exactly-one replacement, distinct indices, signed range, and wide result.
